City of Savannah

Think about the title, this is an American tune.
However, the Session is not entirely devoted to Irish tunes, so it has its place here still.
I know the tune has been Irishised by some performers but the original is a late Nineteeth century stage hornpipe like President Garfield and most of the James Hill compositions. They were written for performance in vaudeville/music halls and sound more like Tyneside hornpipes than anything else, though there are good examples from Dublin, London and the States. They would usually be performed on violin or concertina.
Key points of stage hornpipes are lots of dotting, lots of syncopations and flasshy quaver runs. Playing them in the more flattened Irish style loses a lot of the characteristics
Noel Jackson
Angels of the North

Savannah, Georgia

The City is also ‘Savannah’ in Georgia in the Southeast USA, just above that popular trailer park, swamp and Disney World called ‘Florida’. Savannah was a cultural centre for the South in the 19th Century and it can still hold its own…and there’s damned good fishing along the Savannah River… There is a lot of beauty there if you want a change from the usual Florida holiday. While Aberystwyth is the centre of the world for some, Savannah is for others.

Re: City Of Savannah

Interesting exchange above on the provenance of this tune: it’s credited here to one Frank Livingston. Any information about him, anyone? Irish? American?

I came across it in ‘A collection of the Dance Music of Ireland’ (Ossian Publications 1988) originally compiled in 1965 by Pat McNulty, who I believe is/was a piper - so he, at any rate, considered that it fell within the ITM category. I picked up the habit from a concertinist friend of mine of playing it with The Poppy Leaf. (https://thesession.org/tunes/1058). They make a good pair. If of interest, there are 2-part arrangements of both at: http://www.rudemex.co.uk/library/Alphabetical/City%20of%20Savannah%20(a).pdf and: http://www.rudemex.co.uk/library/Alphabetical/Poppy%20Leaf,%20The%20(a).pdf

Re: City Of Savannah

It’s also in the Kerr’s Merry Melodies collection (1870s), but they may have got it from one of Elias Howe’s collections in the first place. I believe Frank Livingston was American, and there are more of his compositions in Ryan’s mammoth Collection (later republished as “Cole’s 1000 Fiddle Tunes”). Other tunes attributed to Livingstone include “The California Reel” “The Post Horn Reel” “General Longstreet’s Reel” The Golden Gate Reel“ ”The Recreation Reel“ ”The Indian River Hornpipe“ ”The irish American Jig“ ”Get On de Train Jig“ ”The Mountain Sprite“ (jig), ”The Mississippi Hornpipe“ ”Wade Hampton’s Hornpipe“ ”Georgia Crackers“ ”Florida Crackers“ ”The Louisville Clog“ ”The Cincinnati Clog", etc, etc.

According to http://www.ibiblio.org/fiddlers/ryan1.htm Livingston was a New York songwriter who also wrote (and possibly performed) fiddle tunes.

Re: City Of Savannah

Pauline Cato, if I remember correctly, said it was named for a steamship that held the speed record for transatlantic crossings in the 19th century. I like the romance of that version better than a rebel frigate or blockade runner. The city is beautiful, but, coming from a maritime family, I prefer the “fast packet” relationship. But not the nuclear-powered cargo ship “Savannah” from the early 1960s. That ship was too expensive to run, at least safely, and only sailed a few times, if at all.
